title: Armenia and Azerbaijan publish the 17-point text of the initialed peace agreement
body:
On Monday, 11 August 2025 the foreign ministries of Azerbaijan and Armenia shared the text of a 17-point peace agreement that their foreign ministers had initialed on Friday, 8 August, during a trilateral summit at the White House with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, US President Donald Trump and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan.

Under the text, both countries recognise the borders of the former Soviet Azerbaijani and Armenian republics as their mutual boundary. Neither has territorial claims against the other or will raise them in future, and each will refrain from using or threatening force against the other's territorial integrity or political independence and from interfering in its internal affairs. Neither will deploy third-party forces along the border. Diplomatic relations will be established once both exchange instruments of ratification, after which they will negotiate to delimit and demarcate their border.

A bilateral commission will oversee implementation, and mutual claims in international courts will be withdrawn within a month after the agreement enters into force. The Azerbaijani, Armenian and English texts are equally authentic, with the English text prevailing in any divergence. The deal takes effect after both sides exchange notifications that their internal procedures are complete. Azerbaijan said a draft OSCE Ministerial Council decision on closing the OSCE Minsk Group was circulated among member states the same Monday.
